import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 226

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/226](https://www.erdosproblems.com/226)
- [BaSc70] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., *Entire functions mapping
  countable dense subsets of the reals onto each other monotonically*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (2) (1970), 620--626.
- [BaSc71] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., *Entire functions mapping
  arbitrary countable dense sets and their complements onto each other*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (2) (1971/72), 482--488.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., *Research problems in function theory: new problems*.
  (1974), 155--180.
-/

namespace Erdos226

/-- A real function preserves rationality. -/
def PreservesRationality (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ) ↔ f x ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ)

/--
Is there an entire non-linear function $f$ such that, for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$, $x$ is rational if and only if $f(x)$ is?

Barth and Schneider [BaSc70] proved the stronger result for countable dense subsets of
$\mathbb{R}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos226.lean"]
theorem erdos_226 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ F : ℂ → ℂ, Differentiable ℂ F ∧ (∀ x : ℝ, (F x).im = 0) ∧
      (∀ g : AffineMap ℝ ℝ ℝ, (fun x : ℝ => (F x).re) ≠ g) ∧
      PreservesRationality (fun x : ℝ => (F x).re) := by
  sorry

end Erdos226

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly requires F to be real-valued on real inputs, expresses rationality using its real part, and excludes real affine maps on that restriction rather than directly excluding complex affine entire functions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source's rationality condition implies F(ℚ) ⊆ ℚ. Since an entire function is continuous and ℚ is dense in ℝ, its imaginary part vanishes on all real inputs. Thus rationality of F(x) is equivalent to rationality of its real part. Every AffineMap ℝ ℝ ℝ is exactly x ↦ ax+b. If the real restriction of a real-valued entire F has this form, the complex identity theorem gives F(z)=az+b everywhere; conversely, a complex affine function has an affine real-part restriction. The complete witness predicates, and hence the existential statements, were proved equivalent in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the problem's sorry theorem.

review.notes: Checked both declarations. PreservesRationality is precisely the required biconditional, and answer(True) has the correct scope and polarity. Lean boundary tests covered rational inputs 0 and ±1, the identity, constants, and squaring (which fails the reverse implication at √2). The equivalence proofs compile and depend only on standard axioms. The source agrees with the solved/affirmative/Lean-verified metadata. Original Barth–Schneider full texts and the 1974 Hayman chapter were inaccessible; their relevant results were corroborated by the accessible Hayman–Lingham account. The linked formal proof states an equivalent result and contains no textual sorry or custom axioms, but I could not replay it unchanged: it targets Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1, whereas the sandbox provides 4.33.1. This compatibility limitation is not evidence of a mathematical or status defect.
